title: Bicol Purple taro (Bicol purple gabi): Characteristics
metaDescription: Bicol Purple taro is a local taro variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Bicol Purple taro is a local taro variety, also sold or known as Bicol purple gabi. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from local Bicol cultivar selected by CBSUA.

heroImage.alt: Kamote vines on long raised ridges in San Rafael, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Bicol Purple taro is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Bicol purple gabi, this is the same taro. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [taro variety finder](/crop-varieties/taro), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).
Key facts about Bicol Purple taro

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources
rows: local Bicol cultivar selected by CBSUA

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit taro fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
It is recommended corms and leaves for food, taro flour, starch and milk under development.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Where:** Camarines Sur (Calabanga, Pili) and the Bicol region.
**Uses:** Corms and leaves for food, taro flour, starch and milk under development.
Very good leaves and corms in upland and lowland field trials.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: picked by CBSUA from ten local cultivars as a candidate for NSIC registration. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Bicol Purple taro
Gabi grows in wet lowland or on upland beds. Pick a variety for the land you have, and for the corm, the leaves or both.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Bicol purple gabi the same as Bicol Purple?
items.a: Yes. Bicol purple gabi is another name for Bicol Purple. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Bicol Purple?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
